title: Introduce inference-pipeline health index and stable alert anchors
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Production customers reported hard-to-interpret alert storms where token-cost and latency alerts fired in rapid succession without a clear initiation signal. This PR introduces an inference-pipeline health index (IPI) and a small set of "stable alert anchors" that act as high-signal priors for alert correlation and suppression. Goal: reduce alert churn while preserving detection of real regressions, provide a single-number health signal for dashboards and runbooks, and enable anchored trace sampling to surface representative traces for SREs and on-call engineers.

What this changes (high level):
- Adds a new metric series 'inference.pipeline_health' computed from a weighted combination of per-stage success/failure ratios, median stage latency, token-queue-depth, and recent kv-cache-miss-rate. Weights are configurable via config/telemetry/pipeline_health.yaml.
- Implements 'stable alert anchors' for the cost/latency alerting pipeline: a small set of tenant+route anchors whose sampled traces are retained longer and used to stabilize alert thresholds. Anchors are chosen via a lightweight ranker and can be overridden by ops.
- Adds a trace sampler hook that uses the IPI + anchor mapping to increase sample probability for traces that materially move the index; these traces are annotated with anchor_id and index_delta.
- Dashboard: new Pipeline Health dashboard (dashboards/pipeline_health.json) with a top-level IPI sparkline, anchor list, and per-stage diagnostic rows.
- Alerting: new alert rules that roll up from token/latency SLOs into the IPI-based incident policy; includes automated cooldown and scoped suppression if a single anchor causes repeated noise.

Description and design notes:
- The IPI is intentionally coarse: values in [0,100] where 100 = green. It is computed in the telemetry pipeline (service: telemetry/ingest) as a streaming aggregation to avoid adding synchronous latency to inference paths. The aggregator uses exp-decay windows to be responsive to regressions while smoothing burst noise.
- Anchors are scored using a 'stability' heuristic (variance in latency/cost over the last 24h) and a 'representativeness' heuristic (share of similar invocation shapes). The algorithm is conservative by default to minimize churn in anchor selection.
- Sampling hook lives in tracing/trace-sampler and requires a small config bump in the tracing agent; when IPI delta for an invocation passes a threshold, trace retention TTL is bumped and the trace is tagged with anchor metadata.
- Rollout: feature gated behind 'telemetry.pipeline_health.enabled' and default-off for tenants with fewer than 1000 invocations/day to avoid biasing small customers.

Checklist: 
- [x] Compute IPI in streaming telemetry aggregator with configurable weights
- [x] Anchor selection service and basic API (list/add/remove)
- [x] Trace sampler hook + metadata annotations
- [x] Pipeline Health dashboard seeded with panels
- [x] New alerting policies wired to IPI with cooldown logic
- [x] End-to-end tests for index calculation and sampler gating
- [x] E2E load test run to validate no added p99 latency regression

Commits summary:
- 7c1a2d3: telemetry: add pipeline health index aggregator and config
- 3b4d5e6: tracing: anchor-aware trace sampler and annotations
- a1b2c3d: dashboard: add pipeline_health dashboard JSON and import script
- d4e5f6a: alerts: add IPI-based alert rules and cooldown logic
- e7f8a9b: tests: unit + integration tests for index and sampler

Files changed (high level):
- telemetry/aggregators/pipeline_health.py (new)
- config/telemetry/pipeline_health.yaml (new configurable weights)
- tracing/trace_sampler/anchor_hook.py (new)
- dashboards/pipeline_health.json (new)
- alerts/pipeline_health_rules.yaml (new)
- tests/telemetry/test_pipeline_health.py (new)
- docs/observability/pipeline_health.md (new runbook + design)

Testing and performance: 
- CI: unit, integration and linter passed. Canary e2e load run against staging showed no regression in p99 inference latency (baseline 210ms, canary 213ms under heavy synthetic warmup; within SLA).
- Memory/CPU: aggregator adds ~8MB heap per telemetry ingest worker and a negligible CPU uplift; trace sampler path is async and uses sampling budget tokens to avoid overwhelming storage.
- Alert noise: internal dogfood tenant reduced duplicate alerts by ~32% in the first week of beta when anchors were tuned.

Rollout plan: 
1) Merge behind feature flag 'telemetry.pipeline_health.enabled=false'
2) Enable for internal dogfood and two low-volume customers (gradual enable)
3) Monitor IPI drift and anchor stability metrics for 72h, adjust config weights if any single metric dominates the index
4) Open a changelog entry and announce to SRE/product ops when enabling more tenants

Backward compatibility and breaking changes: 
- No breaking changes to the public API. Traces will include new optional tags (anchor_id, ipi_before, ipi_after). Customers using raw trace schemas will see new fields but should ignore unknown tags.

Runbook excerpt (docs/observability/pipeline_health.md):
- If IPI drops > 20 points and persists > 10 minutes, run 'ipi diagnose <anchor_id>' which will pull top traces and per-stage histograms. Use 'ipi-suggest-fallback' to automatically route traffic to a compatible lower-cost model variant while investigation proceeds.

Release notes: 
- Add a pipeline health index metric to surface a single health signal for inference; introduce anchor-based trace stabilization and new dashboard + alerting policies.

Related work: 
- Complements per-token cost attribution work (ENG-1024) and per-route latency trellising (ENG-1156).
